text.name: eq_help_temperament_2
text.text: Three errors of course (losing the line, leaving the arena or standing still) end the test; finish it for a Temperament boost that grows with your score. A calmer horse sees more of the line ahead and gets more warning of changes. Riding Hall markers give the older routine of legs between letters. Away from an arena, walking and backing up still train a little Temperament, and treats like carrots help too.

text.name: eq_help_temperament_1
text.text: Temperament training is all about teaching your horse control, and it needs a dressage arena: buy one from the shop or set out dressage markers. In a shop arena, ride to A and a test of figures starts: circles, diagonals, serpentines and more, drawn as a gold line on the ground. Stay on the line and change gait or halt where you are told; each movement is marked out of 10.

text.name: eq_help_agility_2
text.text: You lose your multiplier if you don't clear a new obstacle in time or lose too much speed. Jumping without an obstacle gives some training benefit but doesn't raise your multiplier.

text.name: eq_help_agility_1
text.text: Agility is all about clearing jumps, though you can gain a little from cycling through the gaits. Clear obstacles to build an Agility training multiplier, which fades after ten seconds, or sooner if you hit an obstacle.

text.name: eq_shop_dressageArena_function
text.text: A dressage arena with every letter in place. Ride a horse in it to train temperament between the markers.

text.name: eq_shop_courseFlags_function
text.text: Mark any obstacle as a cross country fence. Switch segments with N/M: place a white flag at one end of the obstacle, run the gold line along the ground to its other end, then place a red flag. The line shows only in construction mode; the obstacle itself is what gets jumped.

text.name: eq_shop_showJump_function
text.text: A show jump whose poles fall when your horse hits them and go back up after the round, or once you ride away.

text.name: eq_shop_xcDrop_function
text.text: A plank wall for a cross country drop. Sculpt a bank, place it on the top with the lip at the edge, and its side walls hide the steep slope.

text.name: eq_shop_xcJump_function
text.text: A cross country fence. Its red and white flags mark where to jump.

text.name: eq_shop_xcHidden_function

text.name: eq_help_freestyle_2
text.text: Agility is trained by jumping obstacles to build a combo meter, and Temperament by riding a test in a dressage arena. Stamina and Speed train from riding the gallop well: press H while galloping to learn how.

text.name: eq_help_freestyle_3
text.text: Rather not ride? Hire grooms and trainers on the Staff tab to train your horses each day. The game's animal staff and RLRM's Herdsman only keep them ticking over.

text.name: eq_help_freestyle_4
text.text: Ride before a contest! Every stat you train with its mini game puts your horse in Peak form for this month's events, up to +8 per stat. It doesn't add up over several days: your best session of the month counts.

text.name: eq_help_form_1
text.text: Your own riding does more than train: it puts your horse in Peak form for this month's events. Each stat you worked in its mini game gets up to +8 in every event this month, shown as Peak form here and in the horse's Skills box. Better sessions give a bigger bonus; just riding the gaits gives none.

text.name: eq_help_form_2
text.text: Peak form doesn't add up over the days of a month: each stat keeps your best session. It can even lift a horse past its potential on the day, then wears off once this month's events have run. Staff keep up the daily training, so save your riding for the events that matter.

text.name: eq_help_freestyle_1
text.text: Riding trains your horse's stats, and each stat is trained with its own mini game. All stats can be trained at the same time, but some don't mix well, such as Speed and Temperament. Press Y to switch to a view with better feedback on the stat you want to focus on, or stay in Freestyle for general feedback. The riding bar is still the horse's energy for the day: once it is full, that horse cannot make any more progress until the next day.

text.name: eq_welcome_welcome_1
text.text: Your horses now have skills to train and events to compete in. It all lives in the Realistic Livestock menu, which you can open by pressing R in the Animals menu or Shift+O anywhere.

text.name: eq_welcome_menu_1
text.text: Open the Information tab (the pig with an [i]) to learn about your horses, the Events tab (the rosette) to enter them in events, and the Equestrian Staff tab (two people) to hire grooms and trainers. You can also find Realistic Equestrian's own settings in the Settings tab (the cog).

text.name: eq_welcome_staff_hire
text.text: Hire staff on the Hire tab to look after your horses every day. Grooms train all four stats, clean horses and bring loose ones home. Trainers focus on two stats and coach horses for their events. A vet means fewer injuries and cheaper treatment, and a broker gets you better prices at the dealer. Wages are paid daily, and candidates come and go, so check back for better ones. Everyone uses all their skills, even outside their primary duties, so a lucky all-rounder helps in every way.

text.name: eq_welcome_staff_works
text.text: On Your staff, pick the stables a groom or trainer works in, then either roles or individual horses. Staff are most effective when only working on a few horses each; other horses only get a little of their time. Disable anyone you don't need for half their wage: the change starts at 1 am the next day.

text.name: eq_welcome_info_skills
text.text: Stamina lets a horse go further, Speed makes it faster, Agility helps it jump and turn, and Temperament keeps it calm and obedient. Every skill can be trained, and you'll learn how when you first ride.

text.name: eq_welcome_info_potential
text.text: Potential is how far each skill can grow with training. Young horses learn the fastest, and older horses can lose potential. Potential is only estimated, and even the estimate can be wrong until you have owned the horse for a while.

text.name: eq_welcome_info_roles
text.text: You can give a horse a role with the Role button to help keep track. Grooms and trainers on the Staff tab can work on every horse with a role, or on one horse.

text.name: eq_welcome_info_feed
text.text: Hay is the basic diet. Oats give a minor boost to Stamina and Temperament, barley a moderate boost to Stamina and Agility, and corn a large boost to Speed. Carrots (and apples, if available) give a large boost to Temperament.

text.name: eq_welcome_events_disciplines
text.text: Dressage favours Temperament and Agility, Show Jumping Agility, races Speed and Stamina, and Cross Country and Eventing favour all-rounders.

text.name: eq_welcome_events_transport
text.text: Auto Transport takes your horse to the event for a fee. This can cost much more than regular automatic transport, as your horse could be going much further and you want to get it back! Taking your horses to the animal dealer yourself (Manual Transport) can save a lot of money.

text.name: eq_welcome_events_risks
text.text: Every event has an injury and disease risk, shown before you enter. The Diseases button in the Information tab lets you treat injuries. A horse can also be scratched before an event for failing a Temperament check or for poor health, but you get part of the entry fee back.

text.name: eq_settings_helpPopups_tooltip
text.text: Show again: every welcome and training help popup pops up once more.

text.name: eq_welcome_diseases_treatment
text.text: Most injuries heal on their own but can take a long time! Treating them speeds this up but can get expensive. You can retire an injured horse to keep breeding from it, which makes recovery much cheaper. Some bad injuries can force retirement, and all of this can be changed in the settings.

text.name: eq_train_worn
text.text: Riding bar full: no more training today

text.name: eq_help_gallop_1
text.text: Your horse gallops at three paces. Press W from a canter to start Pushing: fast, but the Exertion bar fills, and faster the higher it gets. Press S to Recover: a slower gallop that brings exertion back down while you keep galloping, quickly from the top third of the bar and the bottom third, slowly through the middle. Press W again to push on. A fitter horse tires more slowly and recovers faster.

text.name: eq_help_gallop_2
text.text: If the bar reaches the red Fatigued section while you are Pushing, your horse drops to a canter and can't gallop again until the bar is empty. To slow to a canter yourself, press S once while Recovering with an empty bar, or double tap S at any time.

text.name: eq_help_gallop_3
text.text: Tap W continually while galloping to Sprint: much faster, and the bar fills slowly at first, then faster and faster, so stop before the line. Ending a Sprint drops to Recovering, and there is no new Sprint until the bar is empty. Only a Sprint can go past the Fatigued line, for one last push to the finish, but a Sprint that ends there leaves your horse Blown and it recovers very slowly until it is back under the line.

text.name: eq_help_gallop_4
text.text: Training: a Sprint trains Speed, and the higher it takes the bar before it ends, the more it is worth: x2 half way to the line, up to x10 just short of it, but only x1 if it ends past the line. Pushing and Recovering train Stamina at the Stamina multiplier, up to x5. Pushing raises it, faster near the top. Recovering in the middle third of the bar lets your horse get its breath back and keeps most of the multiplier, while the top and bottom thirds lose it quickly, and a horse that never gets its breath back gains much more slowly. Fatigued or Blown drops it to x1 and stops Stamina training until the bar is empty.

text.name: eq_ex_hint_locked
text.text: Canter until the bar is empty

text.name: eq_help_stamina_1
text.text: Stamina trains while you Push and Recover at a gallop, at the Stamina multiplier, up to x5. Pushing raises it, and the closer you get to the line the faster it climbs. Recovering lowers it: quickly from the top third of the bar, slowly in the middle third, quickly again in the bottom third.

text.name: eq_help_stamina_2
text.text: So push close to the line, ease off into the middle of the bar and let your horse get its breath back there for a while, then push again. Bouncing between Push and Recover near the top tires your horse without raising the multiplier, and Fatigued or Blown drops it to x1 and stops Stamina training until the bar is empty.

text.name: eq_help_speed_1
text.text: Speed trains while you Sprint: tap W continually while galloping. Every second of a Sprint counts, and when it ends it is multiplied by how high you took the bar: x2 half way to the line, up to x10 just short of it.

text.name: eq_help_speed_2
text.text: A Sprint that ends past the line is worth only x1, so stop tapping (or press S) before the line. After a Sprint your horse has to recover to an empty bar before it can Sprint again.
